doc.title: Danny Barker — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Sidney Bechet in Europe and his soprano saxophone records
summary: Barker explains that Bechet was abroad but his Wild Man Blues and one-man band records made him famous.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Sidney Bechet: the man, the horn, the legend

blocks.x: I was asking you about the . . .
Did you meet Sidney Bechet up there?

You heard of Sidney Bechet. Sidney Bechet is in Europe. You heard, but he had made that famous record where he was running changes when nobody ever heard it. The Wild Man Blues. You ever heard of that?

That was a famous record, was a sensational hit. He played the soprano, which most musicians, saxophone, didn’t fool with, because they say you couldn’t play it in tune. But Sidney Bechet played it in tune, if you want to consider that. And he played it masterful, because he had been a broken-hearted trumpet player, cornet player. He could play a little cornet. He made a record playing all instruments, didn’t he?
Quite a few, yeah. Called his one-man band. Sheik of Araby and some other.
